title: Hexanol, which does not block gap junctions, does not alter head shape

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Hexanol, which does not block gap junctions, does not alter head shape

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In G. dorotocephala, the same 3-day exposure to hexanol, a closely related alcohol that does not efficiently block gap junction channels, does not produce altered head morphologies, consistent with the head-shape change depending on octanol's gap-junction-blocking activity rather than a generalized effect of long-chain alcohols.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.1. Perturbation of Bioelectric Networks Produces Inter-Species Morphological Change

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The same 3-day treatment with the closely related alcohol, hexanol (6-OH), which does not efficiently block gap junction channels, and subsequent regeneration in water for 7 days, did not produce altered morphologies, consistent with the importance of the GJ-blocking activity of octanol, and not some other generalized effect of long-chain alcohols.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “3. Discussion › 3.1. Perturbation of Bioelectric Networks Produces Inter-Species Morphological Change”. Scope: Regenerating G. dorotocephala fragments treated with hexanol versus octanol

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The experimental contrast is direct and can be audited to a limited extent from published results. Its mechanistic interpretation remains incomplete because one negative alcohol control cannot isolate gap-junction blockade.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare blinded altered-head incidence after matched hexanol, octanol, and water exposures, including survival and developmental timing. A null hexanol effect alongside a reproducible octanol effect supports but does not prove gap-junction specificity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Underlying per-worm control data are not clearly deposited.

Hexanol is an imperfect control for all octanol off-target effects.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A same-schedule alcohol control is a direct contrast, and the paper reports no shape change after hexanol. The counts behind that negative result are not deposited. The control also leaves other chemical differences between the two alcohols unseparated, so both the missing counts and that confound block a present-day resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply the same three-day exposure and seven-day water regeneration to matched fragments in hexanol and octanol, and compare rates of non-Girardia head shapes. Hexanol rates at the water-control baseline, with octanol elevated, would support channel-specific dependence; hexanol reproducing the octanol shapes would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Hexanol and octanol differ in properties other than gap-junction potency.

Hexanol group size and shape counts are not in a public table.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: Octanol engages a planarian gap-junction channel better than hexanol does, consistent with the paper's premise that hexanol 'does not efficiently block gap junction channels'.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Receptor: AlphaFold3 (Nebius) model of the smedinx-11 octameric hemichannel (Schmidtea mediterranea innexin, UniProt A7RDN9, residues 1-370). Ligands docked with DiffDock v1.1 (Nebius), 3 seeds x 4 poses each: ethanol (negative), hexanol, heptanol, octanol, carbenoxolone (positive, a documented innexin/pannexin blocker). For each ligand: mean over seeds of the top-pose DiffDock confidence, and fraction of all poses whose centroid lies within 8 A of the channel axis inside the transmembrane span. Supports: octanol confidence exceeds hexanol's by more than 2 x the larger across-seed SD AND octanol's in-pore fraction exceeds hexanol's by >= 0.25, with carbenoxolone ranking above ethanol on confidence.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Refutes: hexanol confidence >= octanol's and hexanol in-pore fraction >= octanol's. Inconclusive (reason 'not-operationalizable'): carbenoxolone does not outrank ethanol, the hexanol/octanol confidence difference is within 2 x the across-seed SD, or the hemichannel model's ipTM < 0.50. Anything else is mixed.

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Tests only the premise that octanol and hexanol differ in gap-junction engagement; the claim's phenotype (no altered head shapes after hexanol) needs new planarian experiments. Alkanol block of gap junctions is thought to act partly through the membrane rather than a defined binding site, and DiffDock confidence is a pose-quality score, not an affinity, so an inconclusive result is a likely and legitimate outcome. Schmidtea mediterranea substitutes for Girardia dorotocephala (both Tricladida; no Girardia innexin sequences are public).
